source.scope: Capture observation/liveness and controlled-spawn creation, plus fail-closed bounded blocking accepted sockets, a total header deadline and accept-synchronized delayed-header/trickle regressions in the synthetic registry fixture. Excludes private native parser/activation and additional GC/fetch feature fixtures.

observed_failure.result: Default-parallel batch15 failed on actual output-tail capture: directchild exit0, output retained, three matching stdout FWRITE descriptors without close-on-exec in sibling process branches.
observed_failure.scope: The record proves matching sibling holders, not an unrestricted inventory or every possible acquisition path.

fix.production: Serialize controlled Command pipe creation and spawn only; release before wait/observation/callback. Retain WNOWAIT liveness-first observation and strict EOF/timeout/lease cleanup.
fix.fixtures: Route all core Command starts through the same boundary. Output fixtures use their existing null-stdin/piped-output defaults; status fixtures inherit stdio. A piped-stdin child barrier verifies overlap independently of a fixed child duration.

private_integration_build.scope: Full tooling workspace tests and all-target Clippy on macOS; Linux configuration compile/lint only. This private integration also includes an unrelated unexposed native Cargo record parser, omitted from this PR. Exact public candidate CI remains required.

creation_gate_and_counter.scope: Final helper source compiled standalone; valid locking/overlap test passes, isolated removal of only the lock acquisition fails with expected test cause and cleanup.

six_mode_storage_development.scope: Private integration includes additional unmerged concurrent fetch/GC features. This PR contains capture core plus the scoped accepted-socket/header-deadline fix; it is not selected SDK qualification.

limitations: Public exact-candidate CI is required before merge.
No Linux full expanded fixture runtime, both-host fresh production, native AROS runtime/memory, RC2 acceptance or SDK publication.
This controls owned starts inside the process; unrelated libraries spawning without the boundary remain outside it.

registry_socket_followup.diagnosis: The old macOS CI log observes BrokenPipe while writing the RejectAll request. Accepted-socket nonblocking inheritance causing premature header parsing/connection closure is an inference, supported by the isolated local counter, not a direct observation of CI socket flags.
registry_socket_followup.local_result: All four exact public standalone fixture tests pass. Removing only accepted-socket blocking fails the accept-synchronized delayed-header test (actual400/expected401, exit101). Replacing only the absolute header deadline with per-read timeouts fails the trickled-header deadline test (exit101). The primary verifies all eight raw streams and the exact public xtask passes all-target strict Clippy offline on macOS.
registry_socket_followup.retained_harness_failures: A1 lock graph and A2 missing core dependency failures preserved. A3 actual commands have expected0/0/101; its postprocessor incorrectly searched stderr for a Rust failure emitted on stdout. Corrected primary readback preserved separately. A4 independently executes the final four-test/two-counter candidate successfully.
registry_socket_followup.qualification: New exact-public-candidate CI required before merge. No old failure erased; no full workspace/SDK/RC2 result inferred from standalone fixture tests.
registry_socket_followup.implementation: Fail closed if blocking-mode or read/write-timeout setup fails; cap header collection by a two-second total deadline and each read by the smaller remaining time/400ms. Delayed headers wait for accepted-stream setup before a50ms pause. Trickle regression uses a180ms explicit deadline against the same helper.
registry_socket_followup.review_resolution: Independent review A1 identified ignored socket-setup errors, absence of a total header deadline and weak delay ordering. The final candidate resolves them; read-only A2 review finds no remaining material issue.
